description: Sustainability looks at the systems that support everyday life — water, food, community, energy and the things we own — and asks how your household and community can meet today’s needs without using up tomorrow’s.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Requirements 2–7 offer choices of options; the options are summarized.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: What sustainability means
requirements.summary: Sustainability in your own words and why it matters to society.

requirements.title: Water
requirements.summary: An option on household water use, why water matters, or flooding and drought.

requirements.title: Food
requirements.summary: An option on how sustainable different foods are, or what limits food availability.

requirements.title: Community
requirements.summary: An option such as sketching a sustainable community or examining a local unsustainable practice.

requirements.title: Energy
requirements.summary: An option on energy sources, household energy use or reducing consumption.

requirements.title: Stuff
requirements.summary: An option on possessions, waste and recycling.

requirements.title: Big-picture topics
requirements.summary: Topics such as global sustainability goals, life-support systems, product life cycles, population, species decline and climate.

requirements.title: Sustainability in practice
requirements.summary: Observing sustainability on a Scouting outing, applying the Scout Oath, Law and Leave No Trace, and choosing household changes.
